correctness.rationale: For connected cubic six-vertex graphs, the neutral BD chain is absorbing and its type-0 fixation harmonic function is #type0/6. Differentiation yields a unique 729-state rational Dirichlet system on each graph with source g(s)=sum over directed edges of pi_u(s)(1_{s_u=0}-1_{s_v=0})/108. The full certificate checks every exact rational equation and all three absorbing boundary values, independently of how certificate values were generated. It also exhausts all 90 balanced labels and verifies all signs and rational multiplicities, with no numerical extrapolation. Limit: first derivative at zero selection, under the exact specified payoff/fitness normalization.

originality.rationale: The precise original output is the complete 90-configuration rational fixation-derivative spectrum for each of the two six-vertex cubic graph topologies under the three-type cyclic BD game. None of the closely matching primary works states the seven-level/two-graph numerical classification. Broader two-type perturbation principles and graph-game pair approximations are acknowledged and distinguished by assumptions and conclusion. Repeated claim- and parameter-specific database and primary literature searches surfaced no covering result; absence of a hit is not itself a novelty proof.
residual_risks: An unpublished or unindexed table for this exact ternary finite RPS model could exist, notwithstanding targeted searches.
The October 2026 source says supplementary information is not yet available in the openly accessible preprint; no claims about its unseen contents are made.

The general weak-selection derivative equation follows standard finite Markov-chain perturbation principles, so mathematical originality attaches to the fully explicit natural finite exact classification, not to the abstract solution method.

value.rationale: Six is the smallest possible population supporting exactly two of each of three strategies; at the same time it is the smallest size with two distinct cubic graph types. Thus the complete pair of 90-state spectra tests the first natural fixed-frequency, fixed-degree topology/placement distinction, not an arbitrary computational slice. The large difference in number of derivative levels, and exact positive/negative reversal while the focal positions stay fixed, are interpretable benchmarks for finite graph evolutionary games and for limits of frequency closure. Neither exact proof nor unindexed status alone is treated as evidence of value. No downstream universal theorem is claimed.
